circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281-kilometer motorsport venue located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, designed by Hermann Tilke and home to Formula One's season-concluding Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. It ranks as the second Middle Eastern Formula One circuit after Bahrain, with Qatar and Saudi Arabia later joining the calendar in the region.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street racing venue located around Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix along with Supercars and supporting race categories. The track holds an FIA Grade 1 licence, making it suitable for top-tier motorsport competition.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit hosted the Austrian Grand Prix during two separate eras, first from 1970 to 1987 under its original name, then again from 1997 to 2003 following a renovation and rebranding. The track underwent significant modifications between these periods, including a shortening of its layout.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan positioned along Baku Boulevard, measuring 6. 003 km per lap and ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The inaugural race there was the 2016 European Grand Prix, followed by the first Azerbaijan Grand Prix in 2017, with both events organized by the Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km facility that hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix and has since accommodated various motorsport categories including GP2 racing and endurance events. The venue, which holds FIA Grade 1 certification and features multiple track configurations, also hosted Australian V8 Supercars between 2006 and 2010 as part of the Desert 400 racing program.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, located near Barcelona in Catalonia, Spain, stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straightaways and diverse corner configurations that make it a versatile test for Formula One machinery. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: This Belgian circuit spanning 7. 004 km near the town of Spa has been hosting Formula One racing since 1950 and currently stages the Belgian Grand Prix annually. The venue has maintained an unbroken presence on the F1 calendar from 1985 onwards, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, this 4. 361 km circuit serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the track has accommodated numerous international motorsport series including world sportscar racing, open-wheel championships, and various NASCAR competitions throughout its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese racing facility gained prominence as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before returning in 2024. The venue has expanded its motorsport calendar to include electric racing events beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone Circuit, located in England near the Northamptonshire villages of Silverstone and Whittlebury, has been the principal venue for the British Grand Prix since hosting the inaugural event in 1948. The 1950 race held there marked the beginning of the World Championship of Drivers, though the British Grand Prix subsequently alternated between three circuits for several decades before returning exclusively to Silverstone in 1987. Beyond Formula One, the track also stages the British round of motorcycle racing's premier championship.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: Located in Mogyoród near Budapest, the Hungaroring is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted Formula One's inaugural grand prix in a Communist-bloc nation when it opened in 1986, constructed in just eight months, faster than any other Formula One venue. The track was built outside the city following government preference over plans for a street circuit in Budapest's largest park, with its inaugural race dedicated to János Drapál, Hungary's pioneering motorcycle racing champion.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Monza in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. The track has hosted the Italian Grand Prix continuously since 1949, except for a 1980 closure for renovation, and earned the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its characteristic long straights and fast corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: The Suzuka Circuit, a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland, hosts major international racing competitions including Formula One and Super Formula championships. Located in Mie Prefecture, the track accommodates up to 155,000 spectators and ranks among the sport's most prestigious racing destinations.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that weaves through Paradise, Nevada, incorporating the famous Las Vegas Boulevard with its iconic hotels and casinos, as well as recognizable venues like MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas. This urban layout creates a unique racing environment that utilizes the actual streets of the entertainment district rather than a purpose-built facility.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez in Mexico City honors two fatal racing drivers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who died in 1962 and 1971 respectively. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix across three separate eras, with the current iteration beginning in 2015 on its modern configuration, now officially called the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary racing venue constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida, measuring 3. 363 miles with 19 turns and an average qualifying pace of approximately 139 mph. Created by specialist circuit designers Apex Circuit Design, this track was built to host the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One calendar starting in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street course that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of Monaco, incorporating roads surrounding the principality's harbour. The track is frequently known by the Monte Carlo name due to the majority of its layout residing within that neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: The Zandvoort circuit is a 4. 259 km Dutch motorsport venue situated in the coastal dunes west of Amsterdam, which resumed hosting Formula One's Dutch Grand Prix in 2021 after a lengthy absence. The facility's relationship with the sport is set to conclude in 2026.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is situated in the outskirts of Lusail, north of Doha, in Qatar. Measuring 5. 419 kilometers with a principal straight spanning 1.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing venue in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late Formula One driver José Carlos Pace. The circuit operates in a counterclockwise direction and also features a karting facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: Located along Jeddah's waterfront on the Red Sea, the Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street-based racing venue that has hosted the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its debut in 2021 and became home to the Formula E Jeddah ePrix starting in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Marina Bay area, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang districts as it traverses city streets.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657 km racing venue features a balanced mix of lengthy straightaways and diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing multiple aspects of driver and vehicle performance. The facility holds FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located near Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the track hosts multiple international racing series including MotoGP, the FIA World Endurance Championship, and NASCAR events, alongside various other motorsport competitions that have rotated through its schedule over the years.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British driver currently racing for Williams in Formula One, competing under Thailand's flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Fernando Alonso, a Spanish driver currently racing for Aston Martin in Formula One, secured two world championship titles during his time with Renault in 2005 and 2006, accumulating 32 Grand Prix victories across his 23-season career. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved significant success in endurance racing, claiming the 2018–19 World Endurance Championship, two Le Mans 24 Hours victories with Toyota, and a Daytona 24 Hours win in 2019, making him uniquely the only driver to win both Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli joined Mercedes for the 2025 Formula One season and has secured six race victories since entering the championship.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, representing the team in the championship.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One as a member of the Audi team, representing his nation in the sport's premier championship.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing over a decade of experience to the grid. During his time with Mercedes, he achieved two consecutive runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship and accumulated 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his 13-season career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor who currently drives for Alpine in Formula One.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve role with Haas in Formula One while actively competing in European Le Mans Series prototype racing. He has participated in seven Grand Prix events between 2024 and 2025.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver achieved a notable victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix during his time with AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar is a French-Algerian racing driver representing France in Formula One competition with Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently competing for Ferrari who has achieved seven World Drivers' Championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. The driver holds multiple circuit records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi, bringing extensive racing experience to the grid. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved significant success in endurance motorsport, securing victory at the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 alongside Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver competing for Ferrari, finished as runner-up in the 2022 World Drivers' Championship and has claimed nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in Formula One.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver competing in endurance racing for BMW's WRT team while also pursuing a part-time NASCAR career with Trackhouse Racing. His Formula One career spanned two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and again in 2022-2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris represents Great Britain on the Formula One grid, currently racing for McLaren where he secured the 2025 Drivers' Championship. The accomplished competitor has claimed 13 Grand Prix victories throughout his eight seasons in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The former Alpine driver achieved a grand prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez, a Mexican driver currently racing for Cadillac in Formula One, finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while with Red Bull. The veteran has accumulated six Grand Prix victories throughout his 15-year career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian racing driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, claiming eight Grand Prix victories during his career. Known by the nickname "the Honey Badger", Ricciardo has since retired from the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish racing driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American racing driver whose Formula One tenure spanned 2023 and 2024. He currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category for Proton Competition, having previously driven in the IMSA SportsCar Championship's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin. He competes at the highest level of international motorsport under his more commonly used name.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese motorsport competitor, has held reserve driver positions within the Red Bull Racing organization across multiple teams. His active Formula One participation spanned from 2021 through 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Max Verstappen is a Dutch-Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing who has secured four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. The 12-season Formula One career of Verstappen includes 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is China's sole Formula One competitor to date, having raced in the championship between 2022 and 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Alpine Racing competes from its Enstone base as Renault's works team since rebranding in 2021 to promote the French automaker's Alpine sports car line. The team achieved a single victory in its Alpine identity when Esteban Ocon won the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, though Renault ended its works team involvement following the 2025 season. Currently powered by Mercedes engines and competing under a French licence, Alpine fields Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has competed in Formula One multiple times throughout its history as a British manufacturer, with its current racing operation organized under AMR GP Limited and competing under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of Italian manufacturer Ferrari, represents the sport's most enduring and accomplished team, competing continuously since the championship's inception in 1950. The squad, nicknamed "the Prancing Horse" after their emblematic symbol, stands as Formula One's longest-running operation and has accumulated the sport's most substantial record of achievement.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed outfit founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas, the squad entered Formula One competition in 2016 and operates under current team principal Ayao Komatsu, who took over from Guenther Steiner in early 2024.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, the Swiss engineering firm established itself in motorsport through endurance racing success, including victory at the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours with Mercedes-Benz. After joining Formula One in 1993, the team operated as an independent constructor through numerous iterations until ceasing operations in 2025, having become the fourth-longest-serving constructor by race entries. Audi acquired the team and its operations in 2024 to serve as the technical foundation for its own Formula One entry.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under corporate sponsorship arrangements. The organization operates as part of the broader McLaren Group structure and is ultimately owned by Bahrain's sovereign wealth fund.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a continuous presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, currently operating as Mercedes-AMG Petronas from its Brackley base under a German racing licence. The team restructured its ownership in 2022 to include equal stakes held by the Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff. The squad is traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows" due to its iconic silver livery heritage.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as one of two teams operated by Red Bull GmbH, alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the team functions as a sister outfit within the Red Bull motorsport structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team operation. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the squad operates as the sister team to Red Bull Racing within the Austrian conglomerate's motorsport portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, operating under an Austrian licence despite being headquartered in England, has been a prominent Formula One outfit since its 2005 establishment under the ownership of Red Bull GmbH. Christian Horner led the team from its inception through 2024, with Laurent Mekies assuming the management role thereafter. The conglomerate also operates Racing Bulls as its second Formula One entry.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, rising from the ashes of Williams's previous failed racing venture. Based at their Grove facility in Oxfordshire, the team competes in the 2026 season as Atlassian Williams F1 Team.
